Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the initial RFP submission. Our procurement and legal teams have a couple of follow-ups specifically on production site-of-record and activation/failover conditions across regions. We want to understand both (a) where customer data can be persisted in normal operation (site-of-record), and (b) which scenarios trigger migration or failover to another region and how data residency is preserved during those flows.

Key asks:
- For EU customers, can Redwood guarantee that inference logs, KV caches, and customer blob artifacts will remain in EU regions only?
- If a customer enables warm-standby in a cross-region configuration, what controls are available to prevent warm-standby writes from leaving the primary jurisdiction until explicit activation?
- Describe the exact conditions (operational, legal, capacity) that would allow Redwood to route traffic or persist data outside the declared site-of-record.
- Provide sample evidence that these controls are operable (config screenshots, SOC2 evidence pointers).

We are on a tight procurement cadence and would appreciate a consolidated response by COB Tue 30 Nov.

Best,
Elena

Elena —

Thank you for the clear list. We can meet the residency guarantees you describe; below is a consolidated summary and a few attachments (detailed matrix + supporting evidence). I copied our infra and product leads so we can include precise operational controls.

Executive summary (short):
- Site-of-record: Customers can designate an explicit site-of-record per account (region selection) for persisted artifacts (logs, KV snapshots, deployed model artifacts). When set to EU, persisted data remains within EU cloud regions under normal operation.
- Warm-standby: We support warm-standby nodes that are read-only by default; writes to warm-standby are blocked until a documented activation workflow completes (see activation_conditions_matrix.xlsx).
- Failover / routing outside site-of-record: Traffic routing or write persistence to a non-site-of-record region can only occur under three narrow, auditable conditions: 1) customer-initiated activation, 2) certified regional evacuation for physical/legal emergency (e.g., court order with global reach), or 3) automatic overflow when explicit capacity SLOs are breached and the customer has opted into cross-region overflow in contract. Each path generates an immutable audit event and optionally a customer-notify webhook.

What I attached: Redwood_Data_Residency_Summary_v1.pdf (summary + architecture diagram); activation_conditions_matrix.xlsx (condition-by-condition controls + required approvals); evidence-sample-soc2.pdf (SOC2 section references and artifact examples).

- We also propose adding a contract clause that prevents cross-region write activation without written customer approval except for legal compulsion.

Aisha / Laura — quick technical addendum to include in the consolidated reply:

1) KV cache and ephemeral memory: by default, KV cache and in-memory model state are ephemeral and live on the serving node; they are not written to durable storage. For customers that require no cross-border cache replication, we can disable asynchronous cross-region cache warmup so no transient copies are seeded outside the site-of-record.

2) Audit & telemetry retention: telemetry used for observability (traces, perf logs) can be routed to an EU-only telemetry store per account. We apply token-level redaction rules before any export.

3) Activation workflow: customer activation requires two SAs from the customer admin group plus a Redwood Operator approval (UI + API). When activation is accepted, we snapshot affected artifacts and write a time-stamped event to the account's immutable audit log. The audit entry includes the triggering IP, operator id, and a link to the related change request.

4) Emergency legal compulsion: in the rare event of a lawful order requiring data transfer, we will notify customers per contract SLAs and provide a time-bound chronology of the actions taken.

I'll add a short appendix with the CLI/API calls that show how the account-level residency flags are set and how to enable/disable warm-standby writes.

Thanks again for the follow-up. Please find our consolidated response attached and summarized below. We kept the answers compact to align with your procurement checklist; full appendices are in the attachments and the Drive link.

Consolidated summary (final):
- Site-of-record: Redwood supports per-account site-of-record designation (EU/US/APAC). Persisted artifacts (model artifacts, logs, KV snapshots) remain in the designated region during normal operations.
- Warm-standby controls: Warm-standby is configured read-only by default. Writes are blocked until a documented activation workflow completes: two customer admin approvals + Redwood Operator acknowledgement.
- Allowed cross-region activation paths (auditable):
  1) Customer-initiated activation (explicit written/console/API approval) — customer must confirm acceptance via two admin approvals.
  2) Legal compulsion with notice — Redwood will comply with lawful orders; we will provide a time-stamped evidence package and customer notification consistent with contract terms.
  3) Contracted overflow — if the customer has pre-agreed overflow in their order form, Redwood may route writes to the overflow region when capacity SLOs are breached; this is opt-in only.
- Audit & notification: All cross-region or activation events create immutable audit entries, generate customer notifications, and can trigger a webhook to your security mailbox.
